newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas preparing to resume attacks against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hamas preparing to resume attacks against Israel.

text.p: The armed wing of the militant Moslem group Hamas, hit hard by PLO and Israeli crackdowns, said on Friday it would mark the first anniversary of the killing of its master bombmaker by renewing attacks against Israel.

"Our response to the martyrdom of the giant engineer on his first anniversary will be strong, very painful and a major challenge to the state of the Zionist entity with all its army, forces, security and war supplies," it said in a statement faxed to an international news agency.
The Izz el-Deen al-Qassam brigades said it was preparing for "military operations".
Bombmaker Yahya Ayyash was killed last January 5 in Gaza when his booby-trapped cellular telephone exploded. The assassination is widely believed to have been carried out by Israel.
Qassam responded with four suicide bombings in February and March in Israel killing 59 people.
The Palestinian Authority and Israel subsequently launched crackdowns against Hamas, rounding up about 2,000 of the group's supporters.
The Authority destroyed Hamas' infrastructure by taking over mosques once run by the Islamic group and closing down Hamas charity institutions in Gaza and the West Bank.
Qassam said in the statement it was in the process of rebuilding armed cells destroyed earlier this year.

"The Qassam brigades today is living a process of quiet recruitment and preparations to rebuild its ranks and to organise its military cells which had been hit by aggression and oppression," the statement said.
It described Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as "the dwarf of the Zionist government".
Hamas planned to hold a rally in the Gaza Strip town of Khan Younis later on Friday to mark the ninth anniversary of its founding.
In Damascus, George Habash, leader of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, pledged more attacks on Israelis and urged Palestinians to launch a fresh uprising against the Jewish state.
On Thursday the PFLP, which has strong support in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, claimed responsibility for Wednesday's killing of a Jewish settler and her 12-year-old son in the West Bank.
